input.question: Which person or organization did Dirk Smits work for?

documents.text:
Dirk Smits

Dirk Smits is a renowned researcher in the field of medical sciences, best known for his contributions to the University of North Carolina School of Medicine. Early Career

Smits received his Ph.D. in Biochemistry from the University of Amsterdam in 2005. His dissertation, titled "The Role of Enzyme Kinetics in Cellular Metabolism," was widely acclaimed and laid the foundation for his future research endeavors. University of North Carolina School of Medicine (2010-2015)

In 2010, Smits joined the University of North Carolina School of Medicine as a research associate in the Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics. During his tenure, he collaborated with Dr. Maria Rodriguez, a prominent researcher in the field of cancer biology, on a series of studies investigating the molecular mechanisms underlying tumorigenesis. One of the most notable studies conducted by Smits and Rodriguez was published in the journal Nature Medicine in 2012. The study, titled "Inhibition of Tumor Growth by Small Molecule Inhibitors of the PI3K\/Akt Signaling Pathway," demonstrated the efficacy of novel small molecule inhibitors in suppressing tumor growth in vitro and in vivo. [1]

Smits' work at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine also focused on the development of novel diagnostic tools for cancer detection. In 2014, he co-authored a study published in the journal Cancer Research, which described the development of a novel biosensor for the detection of circulating tumor cells in peripheral blood. [2]

Awards and Honors

Smits' contributions to the field of medical research were recognized with the prestigious "Rising Star in Cancer Research" award, presented by the American Association for Cancer Research in 2013. References

[1] Rodriguez, M., Smits, D., et al. (2012). Inhibition of Tumor Growth by Small Molecule Inhibitors of the PI3K\/Akt Signaling Pathway. Nature Medicine, 18(10), 1431-1438. [2] Smits, D., Lee, J., et al. (2014). Development of a Novel Biosensor for the Detection of Circulating Tumor Cells in Peripheral Blood. Cancer Research, 74(19), 5321-5330.
